sources.note: Dalhousie University Faculty of Graduate Studies' own page for the Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES), on the dal.ca awarding-body domain; contains value, deadlines, description, award conditions, eligibility criteria and application overview

Dalhousie FGS doctoral scholarships, bursaries and awards index, which lists the DRES card as 'Doctoral • Entrance scholarship • Canadian and international students • $35,000 per year • Up to four years' and links to the page above

awarding_body.detail: The page is on dal.ca under Faculty of Graduate Studies > Finance your studies > Scholarships and bursaries, and its footer identifies Dalhousie University's Faculty of Graduate Studies as the owning unit. The page describes the scheme as Dalhousie's own scholarship, established in 2024. It is the awarding body's own page, not an aggregator, news article or mirror.
awarding_body.quote: Established in 2024, the Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES) attracts and supports exceptional new PhD students at Dalhousie University.

deadline.detail: The page publishes two rounds that match the record exactly: round one October 16, 2026 at midnight AT (four days away as of the 12 October 2026 check, so this cycle is currently open) and round two, opening December 1, 2026 with submissions due January 31, 2027 at midnight AT. Round one offers are to be sent by email by December 2, 2026. No past-deadline state on the page.
deadline.quote: Deadlines: Round one – October 16, 2026 at midnight AT / Round two – opens December 1, 2026 – submissions due January 31, 2027 at midnight AT

eligibility.detail: All distinct eligibility claims in the record are confirmed: intent to start (enrol in or transfer to) a Dalhousie PhD between January 2027 and January 2028 (open to both Canadian and international applicants, stated in the 'at a glance' box and repeated in the index card), and the achievement/leadership/impact criteria are quoted verbatim. Funds are only administered after admission and registration, and applicants transferring from a master's to a PhD must apply for a doctoral scholarship before officially transferring.
eligibility.quote: You must have an intent to start (enroll in or transfer to) a PhD program at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028. ... To be successful in receiving DRES funding, applicants must demonstrate outstanding research achievement, exceptional leadership potential, and the capacity to generate significant regional, national, or international impact through their research.

funding.detail: The record's 'Stipend' funding type is consistent with the page: the award is a cash scholarship of $35,000 per year for up to four years (up to 48 months, not past the end of the fourth year), assembled from $28,000 from Graduate Studies plus $7,000 from the supervisor/program. It is not represented as 'fully funded' and does not cover tuition. DRES holders must apply to the Tri-agency CGRS-D competition within their first two PhD years; on winning CGRS-D ($40,000/yr) the DRES becomes honorary, and DRES plus Killam is topped up to the Killam value of $42,000 per year. Additional stipends beyond the award value can be negotiated with the supervisor/program. Annual report due to fgs.slo@dal.ca by July 31 each year the award is held.
funding.quote: This scholarship is valued at $35,000 per year for up to four years provided the award holder maintains eligibility and will include funding from a combination of sources. $28,000 of this award will be provided by Graduate Studies, while the remaining $7000 will be provided by your supervisor and/or program of study.

degree_levels.detail: The award is doctoral only: the 'at a glance' box states 'Degree level: Doctoral', the scholarship is described as supporting new PhD students, and the FGS doctoral index card repeats 'Doctoral'. Matches the record's 'PhD'.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Round one – October 16, 2026 at midnight AT; Round two – opens December 1, 2026 – submissions due January 31, 2027 at midnight AT
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Verified live on 12 October 2026 against Dalhousie FGS' own DRES page (plus the doctoral scholarships index card). Round-one deadline of 16 October 2026 at midnight AT is four days out, so the cycle is open; round two opens 1 December 2026 and closes 31 January 2027. Apply via a CGRS-D application (auto-considered) or, for non-Tri-agency applicants, the FGS Scholarship Management Platform under 'Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027'. Only one application per candidate is reviewed; duplicates are disqualified. Re-check the deadline line before the next cycle since round dates roll over annually. $35,000/yr for up to four years ($28,000 FGS + $7,000 supervisor/program), not tuition coverage.
